item.title: The Loneliness of Being Iranian in the Diaspora
item.description: A grandmother dies in Iran and the family grieves over FaceTime. On the layer of immigrant grief no one talks about, on the hypocrisy of a media that discovers Iranian human rights but never Palestinian ones, and on the right not to speak for everyone.
item.author: Elaheh Farmand

item.title: Venezuela: It's Much More Than Oil
item.description: Wars for oil and wars for alternative energy are the same war. On the Caracazo, the racial structure that made Venezuela vulnerable, and why a genuine solution requires degrowth in the rich world rather than only the arrest of a president.
item.author: Don Fitz

item.title: Abduction in Caracas
item.description: Two decades before US forces seized Nicolás Maduro, Hugo Chávez predicted the method: the Noriega formula, a narco-trafficking indictment, and then anything goes. What the abduction reveals about Washington, about the Bolivarian regime's own hollowing out, and about what may come next for Cuba.
item.author: Tariq Ali

item.title: Ms Maxwell and The Art of The Deal
item.description: A satirical catalogue of demands, in which a prisoner's terms for silence expand until they take in the whole apparatus — the agencies, the bases, the tariffs, the burial with honours.
item.author: Raymond Nat Turner

item.title: The Proof is in the Pudding: A Few Comments on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics
item.description: From the 1953 formulation of "Common Prosperity" through Deng's market turn to Xi's New Era: an account of how the CPC has adapted Marxism to concrete conditions, and what "advanced socialism" by 2049 would require.
item.author: Gary Olson

item.title: "The Days of the United States Propping Up the Entire World Order Like Atlas Are Over."
item.description: A quick reading of the new National Security Strategy: ghoulish, repetitious, sometimes incoherent — and refreshingly honest. The ideological cover is gone, and what is left is a document that quietly concedes American decline.
item.author: Gary Olson

item.title: Sorry, White Nationalists
item.description: Whiteness is an objectively meaningless construct with a checkered history — and the genetic record is unkind to those who invoke it. Ancient DNA shows most Europeans were dark-skinned until the first millennium BC.
item.author: Juan R. I. Cole

item.title: Mass Murder as "Public Service" in "Our Democracy"
item.description: Elliott Abrams is back, urging Trump to finish the job in Venezuela. A record — El Salvador, Guatemala, Nicaragua, Iran-Contra — and the 1995 Charlie Rose exchange with Allan Nairn, reproduced in full.
item.author: Michael Smith

item.title: Larry Summers, Epstein, and the "End Game" Memo
item.description: The Epstein emails brought Summers down. This is the other story: the 1997 memo, the WTO Financial Services Agreement, structural adjustment, the "IMF riots", and the foreclosure moratorium that never happened.
item.author: Greg Palast

item.title: Mokhiber on UN Security Council Abomination
item.description: Resolution 2803 hands control of Gaza to a US-chaired "Board of Peace" and a proxy occupation force, implicitly rejects a series of ICJ findings, and grants Washington a veto over Palestinian self-determination. In one minute of voting, the Security Council lost all legitimacy.
item.author: Craig Mokhiber

item.title: The UN Has Voted to Put the Occupation of Iraq in Charge of Gaza
item.description: The Security Council has voted for an Orwellian "Peace Board" concocted by Donald Trump and run by Tony Blair. A to-do list for anyone unwilling to accept the normalization of not just genocide but colonialism.
item.author: David Swanson

item.title: The People of Ecuador Reject the Return of US Military Bases
item.description: More than 60% of Ecuadorians opposed lifting the ban on foreign bases and rewriting the 2008 Montecristi Constitution — blocking the US military's return to Manta just as the USS Gerald R Ford reached the Caribbean.
item.author: Progressive International Observatory

item.title: Doomed, Not Domed?
item.description: The United States has spent more than $350 billion on missile defence since Reagan without ever conducting a realistic test. Who stands to profit from the Golden Dome, and why it is likely to accelerate the arms race it claims to end.
item.author: Ashley Gate and William D. Hartung

item.title: Let the Sudanese People Walk Toward Peace
item.description: Red alert no. 21. What is happening on the ground, why the SAF and the RSF are fighting, and the six elements a path toward peace would require — beginning with a monitored ceasefire under the leadership of the Resistance Committees.
item.comments: Republished from Tricontinental: Institute for Social Research
item.author: Vijay Prashad

item.title: A Calculated Attempt to Erase the Horizon of Palestinian Liberation
item.description: The resolution installs two bodies with sweeping authority over Gaza's political, economic and security life, neither accountable to Palestinians. A statement rejecting it and calling on progressive forces to name it for what it is.
item.author: Cabinet of the Progressive International

item.title: The Return Home
item.description: On domicide as one of the most powerful tools of genocide — the retraction of yesterday, the threat on today — and on the Sameer Project's campaign to help people return north to homes that are almost certainly gone.
item.author: Maura Finkelstein

item.title: Trump: Sincerity and Verisimilitude
item.description: Trump threatens Nigeria on behalf of persecuted Christians. Three questions about the sincerity of that concern, and one word that ties the examples together.
item.author: Kim Petersen

item.title: Some Thoughts on Trump's Gaza 'Peace Plan'
item.description: The plan's clauses look comprehensive, and it has already produced a ceasefire. But it avoids the central question — the political rights of Palestinians and a sovereign Palestinian state — and mistakes the silencing of guns for peace.
item.author: Faramarz Farbod

item.title: Gaza Tribunal Jury of Conscience
item.description: The concluding statement of the Gaza Tribunal's Jury of Conscience, naming and defining the constituent crimes — domicide, ecocide, reprocide, scholasticide, politicide — and finding Western governments and non-state actors complicit.
item.author: The Jury of Conscience

item.title: AI for War: Big Tech Empowering Israel's Crimes and Occupation
item.description: A policy brief on Project Nimbus, Lavender and the Gospel, and the regulatory vacuum in which commercial AI has become targeting infrastructure — with recommendations for civil society, legal advocates and tech workers.
item.comments: Republished from Al-Shabaka (The Palestinian Policy Network)
item.author: Marwa Fatafta

item.title: AI's Grand Circus
item.description: Every era sells its miracle: the mortgage, the modem, the model. On the AI boom as a moral decision disguised as market logic, and on what $109 billion of private investment could otherwise have bought.
item.author: Democracy At Work

item.title: The Environmental Crisis Is a Capitalist Crisis
item.description: A dossier on the class character of the environmental crisis: why green capitalism cannot solve a crisis capitalism created, and a minimum agenda — seven headings, drawn up with Brazil's Landless Workers' Movement — for confronting it.
item.comments: Republished from Tricontinental: Institute for Social Research
item.author: Tricontinental: Institute for Social Research

item.title: My Testimony at the Gaza Tribunal in Istanbul
item.description: Testimony delivered as an expert witness on university complicity in genocide, organised around three features: investments, partnerships, and the silencing of dissent. The author is one of the sixty-one faculty recorded as having faced retaliation for advocating for Palestine.
item.author: Maura Finkelstein
